changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders who have already pulled their own decline data, open the acceptance conversation with their own numbers: 'Here are your approvals, market by market, and why.' Use 'approvals', not 'authorization'. Answer 'what's mine' before naming any product. Move the average uplift to a footnote and do not use it as the headline.
changes.why: The rep led with the Authorization Boost deck and the average uplift, and the buyer rejected it out loud ('that's an average. What's mine?'; 'I can't take an average to my CFO.'), so the line backfired with this kind of buyer.

changes.change: Write a plain, market-by-market position for reps on 'local acquiring' that answers the buyer's 'Local cards, local rails' framing country by country. Pair it with an offer to run our own country-level approval analysis on the customer's traffic before a competitor's test sets the terms of the comparison.
changes.why: Adyen's by-country test on the customer's own traffic made 'local acquiring' the frame for the deal, and the rep said she didn't know what she'd have pitched against it, so we had no line for the question that decided the deal.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For payments leaders, lead support messaging with a named person at Stripe who reviews your approvals with you every month, instead of response-time tiers.
changes.why: The buyer asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, which is an ownership question that tiered response times do not answer.

changes.change: Add a proof point the payments leader can take to his CFO: his approval gap by market, stated in money terms as 'Money left on the table', built on his own data rather than an average.
changes.why: The payments leader recommended the decision and the CFO approved it, and he told us he couldn't take an average to his CFO, so he needed his own numbers in money terms to carry our case upstairs.
